tasks.note: Prompt said control room / sci-fi / holographic displays; output was an outdoor garden with plants, a bird and a water bottle. The reference photo is a bearded man outdoors, so the IMAGE_EDIT/IPAdapter path imported his background with his face. Identity transfer wanted, setting transfer not. Investigate weight_type and end_at, then edit-workflow denoise, then masking - one change at a time. Partially overlaps T10, whose deferral no longer blocks it. | STEP 1 DONE 2026-07-31: the latent is EmptyLatentImage with start_at_step 0, so this is pure text-to-image and the garden was NOT an img2img latent. Cause is IPAdapter strength: ip-adapter-PLUS transfers composition, background and style, at weight 0.8 / ease out / end_at 0.8 / K+V - effectively 'make an image like this photo', and the reference was shot outdoors. Swapped character and character-multi workflows to ip-adapter-plus-FACE_sdxl_vit-h, which was already installed. Weights left untouched deliberately so the adapter swap can be attributed alone. Inpaint left alone: it masks the region so background transfer is contained, and its weights (0.85 / linear / 1.0) were tuned separately. tasks.name: Switchable model profiles, selected by content
tasks.note: Plumbing exists: comfyui.py:1000-1012 resolves a per-gen-type handler carrying workflow AND model, and set_main_model (:190) overwrites ckpt_name at request time. But a checkpoint is not swappable alone - Pony needs score tags, steps 30, cfg 5-7, DPM++ 2M Karras; sd_xl_turbo needs no score tags, steps ~6, cfg ~1, Euler a (recorded in start-fork.local.bat). tasks.name: Another character's traits leak into the subject's prompt - ROOT CAUSE
tasks.note: Subject was a human male; his prompt carried purple skin, bare chest, Altrusian, geometric patterns on arms, combat trousers, pulse pistol - all another character's. Two consequences: contradictory adjectives on the subject, AND it disarmed a guardrail, because 'bare chest' is an undress phrase so the dressed test suppressed every nudity negative. _drop_secondary_traits matches from anchor tokens and the LLM paraphrases - it writes 'purple skin' where the anchor says 'deep violet skin', and nothing catches 'Altrusian' at all.

tasks.name: Decide 'is the subject dressed' from the subject, not keyword lists
tasks.note: Keyword matching failed twice in one session in both directions: 'bare metal' read as undress, and a leaked 'bare chest' disarmed the negatives for a fully dressed man. Counting garments vs undress phrases is a stopgap that reasons over a prompt describing everyone present, when the question concerns one person. character.visual_wardrobe (anchors.py:41, refreshed every 10 turns) is already a per-character LLM-written answer, and _suppress_stale_wardrobe already establishes the precedence where the scene beats the reinforcement. Scoping the question to the subject makes another character's 'bare chest' unreachable. Escalate to an explicit LLM judgement only when those sources are absent or conflict; keep keyword counting as last-resort fallback only.

tasks.name: Retry when response extraction fails, not only on an empty response
tasks.note: A 12B omitted the required `descriptive` section of a visual prompt; extract_all raised and the visualize aborted before ComfyUI was contacted, so nothing appeared and nothing was queued. The node's `attempts` property was documented and wired as 'retry on empty response' only. Extraction now happens inside the send loop and a malformed response consumes an attempt. Extraction failure gets its own allowance - max(attempts, 2) when a response_spec is present - because generate-visual-asset.json hardcodes attempts: 1, which is exactly the failing path, and raising a shared default would have changed every other graph. Exhausting the attempts re-raises the original ExtractionError rather than continuing with nothing extracted.

tasks.name: Pony rating tags gated on the dressed determination, and cfg 7 -> 8
tasks.note: Payload inspection proved the pipeline was correct and the model was overriding it: the full negative set (nude, naked, topless, bottomless, penis, exposed genitals, pubic hair, undressing, unzipped, open pants, uncensored, nsfw) plus clothing terms and 1boy/male focus were all delivered to ComfyUI, and the image was explicit anyway. The score tags are part of the cause: score_9/score_8_up select for highly-rated booru images and that corpus skews explicit, so the positive prompt carried a bias the anatomy negatives had to fight. Added rating_safe positive and rating_explicit/rating_questionable negative, gated on _subject_is_dressed so a deliberately explicit scene is untouched, and deliberately NOT gated on sex resolution since rating is independent of it and sex resolution has already proven fragile. cfg raised 7 -> 8 on the SDXL paths (character, multi, inpaint, default-sdxl) so negatives bind harder; the qwen/turbo workflows keep cfg 1, which their distilled models require. Also extracted _subject_is_dressed into one helper - it is the seam T16 replaces.

problems.P1: A human male with a bearded male reference image generated as a half-naked female. The positive prompt said '(human male ...:1.3)' - natural language, which the booru-trained CyberRealisticPony_V9 checkpoint barely registers - while 'solo' and 'looking at viewer' sat near the front pulling toward the checkpoint's default subject, a young nude female
problems.P2: There was no sex handling anywhere in the visual pipeline. grep for 1boy/1girl/male focus/gender/sex over agents/visual/ and fork-styles.yaml returned nothing, and _add_species_negatives returns early when species is human, so a human subject had no corrective negatives at all
problems.P3: Poses come out generic. 'looking at viewer' is hardcoded in visual-styles.yaml:41 and :57 beside 'solo', sits at roughly token 20, and directly contradicts an action like leaning over a console
problems.P4: The prompt runs far past useful attention. image_max_tokens is 250 against a DEFAULT_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS of 77; the observed prompt measured ~196 tokens with the action words near token 95, and style.py:39 already records that beyond ~155 tokens roughly half the prompt is past where the encoder meaningfully attends
problems.P5: The action is atomised and unweighted. 'Leaning over the console' arrives as 'standing, lean, hands hovering, interface' with the subject-object relationship destroyed, while the appearance anchor carries :1.3 and the action carries nothing. Roughly 40 tokens are unrenderable abstractions crowding out what does draw
problems.P6: Nudity negatives were incomplete: a subject wearing jeans and a tank top was rendered with trousers open and genitals exposed, which 'nude, naked, topless' do not describe
problems.P7: The reference image's background leaks into the generation - a reactor-room prompt produced an outdoor garden, because the reference photo was taken outdoors
problems.P8: Another character's traits leak into the subject's prompt because _drop_secondary_traits matches anchor tokens while the LLM paraphrases them; this also disarmed the nudity negatives, since the leaked 'bare chest' read as undress intent
problems.P9: Sex conditioning silently did nothing whenever the LLM paraphrased the anchor, because it read _primary_character, which _primary_and_secondary only sets after confirming the anchor's own wording appears in the prompt
problems.P10: IPAdapter was overriding the text conditioning: ip-adapter-plus at weight 0.8, ease out, end_at 0.8, K+V transfers composition and background as well as identity, so an outdoor reference photo put a reactor-room scene in a garden and suppressed prompt detail
problems.P11: A malformed LLM response aborted the whole visualize action, because retries covered only empty responses - not responses missing a required section
problems.P12: The Pony score tags bias toward explicit output: score_9/score_8_up select for highly-rated booru images, a corpus that skews explicit, so the positive prompt fought its own negatives

decisions: Sex is expressed as booru tags (1boy / male focus / 1girl), not natural language. The checkpoint family is tag-trained; 'human male' carries little signal. This is the same principle visual-reference-closure recorded for negatives, applied to the positive, which nobody had done.

Sex tags go at the FRONT of the prompt. Attention thins across the prompt and a tag sitting behind 'solo, looking at viewer' does not hold. They are also added before _trim_to_budget so they are budgeted rather than squeezed out.
Ambiguous or absent gender adds nothing. Character.gender is free-form; a wrong tag actively fights the prompt, which is worse than no tag.
Word-boundary matching on gender is mandatory: 'male' is a substring of 'female' and 'man' of 'woman', so naive substring tests invert the sex.
Nudity negatives are conditional on the prompt saying the subject is dressed. The scene text is the authority on what they wear, so an undressed scene must not have its own intent negated.
IPAdapter stays untouched until R1-R5 are verified. Changing text conditioning and reference strength together makes any result unattributable.
Not conflated with visual-reference-closure T1/T2, the still-unimplemented duplication guardrails. Same file, different defect.

Undress intent in the prompt suppresses the nudity negatives even when a garment is named. 'unbuttoning his shirt' names a garment while describing its removal; the scene text is the authority in both directions, not just when it says they are dressed.

Model switching is a profile, not a checkpoint name: Pony and SDXL-Turbo need different sampler settings and different style tags, so swapping ckpt_name alone produces mush. Recorded before implementing T14.

Dressed-or-not is decided by weight of evidence rather than a single word, as an interim measure: one leaked undress phrase must not disarm the negatives for a subject wearing four garments, while a deliberate undress beat (one garment, one undress phrase) still wins on a tie.

The keyword lists are acknowledged as the wrong instrument (user, 2026-07-31). T16 replaces them with the per-character visual_wardrobe reinforcement, which is already LLM-written and already refreshed on an interval, rather than adding a per-image LLM call for a question that is answered elsewhere.

IPAdapter fix starts with the model, not the weights: ip-adapter-plus-face was already installed and is the variant intended for identity-without-composition. Weights stay at 0.8/ease out/0.8 for now so the swap can be attributed on its own.

Extraction failure gets its own retry allowance rather than raising the shared `attempts` default, because generate-visual-asset.json pins attempts: 1 and changing the default would alter every other graph.

Rating tags are gated on the dressed determination but NOT on sex resolution. Rating is independent of sex, and sex resolution has failed twice already - coupling them would risk losing the rating control too.
cfg raised to 8 only on the SDXL/Pony workflows. qwen_image, qwen_image_edit and z_image_turbo keep cfg 1 because their distilled models require it; raising it there would wreck them.
